forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred over New South Wales will drift east over the Tasman Sea today allowing a cold front to move across the Bight. The front is forecast to continue to move east across southern South Australia on Tuesday, followed by a new high pressure system moving into the Bight on Wednesday. This new high is expected to move slowly east to be over Victoria later this week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning frost patches about the Pastoral districts. Morning fog patches about the agricultural area. Mostly dry morning, with showers developing about southern coastal districts during the afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures near average. North to northwesterly winds, becoming fresh during the day in the south. North to northwesterly winds, freshening about the south, ahead of a westerly change across the Nullarbor later.

Morning frost patches about the northwest. Showers about the southern agricultural area and west coast, extending to the northern agricultural area and possibly the south of the Pastoral districts during the day. Possible small hail with showers in the far southeast. Maximum temperatures below average in the west, near average elsewhere. North to northwesterly, shifting southwest to southerly from the west during the day and becoming fresh about the southeast in the afternoon.

Isolated showers about the coasts and ranges, becoming less likely during the afternoon and evening. Possible small hail with showers in the far southeast. Maximum temperatures below average. Southwest to southeasterly winds.

text.p: Morning frost patches about the Flinders Ranges. Mostly dry day. Maximum temperatures below average. Light winds across the south, east to southeasterly winds in the north.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: Less than 2 mm about the northern agricultural area and south of the Pastoral districts, increasing to 2 to 10 mm about the southern agricultural area, with falls of 5 to 15 mm possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges.
